text: Mostly because of memories, I think. An old ticket or a child's first drawing is worthless to anyone else, but for the owner it can bring back a whole period of their life. Some people also keep things out of a sense of duty — for example, they feel guilty throwing away a gift, even if they never use it. So it's usually about emotions rather than logic.

tips.en: Mostly because of gives the view first, then an example.
tips.kk: Mostly because of — ұстаным бірден, сосын мысал.
tips.ru: Mostly because of — позиция сразу, потом пример.
tips.example: An old ticket or a child's first drawing is worthless to anyone else

tips.en: Out of a sense of duty adds a deeper explanation.
tips.kk: Out of a sense of duty — тереңірек түсіндірме.
tips.ru: Out of a sense of duty — более глубокое объяснение.
tips.example: keep things out of a sense of duty

questions.followUp: Do you keep things like that?
questions.question: Why do people keep things that have no practical use?

text: In many cases, yes. Online shopping has made buying so easy that people order things with one click and forget about them a week later. I've noticed it myself — my wardrobe is full of clothes I've worn once or twice. That said, I think attitudes are slowly changing, and more young people are getting interested in second-hand shops and owning fewer, better-quality items.

tips.en: With one click is a vivid detail that explains why people own so much.
tips.kk: With one click — нақты дерек заттың неге көп екенін түсіндіреді.
tips.ru: With one click — яркая деталь объясняет, почему вещей так много.
tips.example: people order things with one click and forget about them a week later

tips.en: An example from the speaker's own wardrobe makes the view honest.
tips.kk: Өз киім шкафынан мысал пікірді шынайы етеді.
tips.ru: Пример из своего гардероба делает мнение честным.
tips.example: my wardrobe is full of clothes I've worn once or twice

questions.followUp: Why do they keep buying more?
questions.question: Do you think people today own too many things?

text: Quite strongly, although most people like to think they're immune to it. Modern advertising rarely just describes a product; it sells a lifestyle, suggesting that if you buy these trainers, you'll be fitter or more popular. And now that ads are targeted using our search history, they appear exactly when we're most likely to give in, which makes them far more effective than old TV commercials.

tips.en: Although … immune to it shows the speaker sees below the surface.
tips.kk: Although … immune to it — сөйлеуші тереңірек көреді.
tips.ru: Although … immune to it — говорящий видит глубже.
tips.example: most people like to think they're immune to it

tips.en: Targeted ads versus old TV commercials develops the idea by comparison.
tips.kk: Нысаналы жарнама мен ескі теледидар жарнамасы — ой салыстыру арқылы дамыған.
tips.ru: Таргетированная реклама против старой ТВ-рекламы — мысль развита сравнением.
tips.example: far more effective than old TV commercials

note.en: “Sells an image of how you could live”.

questions.followUp: Are some people more influenced than others?
questions.question: How does advertising influence what people buy?

text: In some ways, definitely. A handmade carpet or a piece of jewellery carries the skill and time of a real person, and no two are exactly alike, which gives them a kind of character. Practically speaking, though, factory-made goods are often more reliable and far cheaper, so for everyday items like kitchen equipment, I'd rather have something mass-produced that simply works.

tips.en: Emotional and practical value — the answer goes beyond a simple yes.
tips.kk: Эмоционалдық және практикалық құндылық — жауап «иә» дегенмен шектелмейді.
tips.ru: Эмоциональная и практическая ценность — ответ не сводится к «да».

tips.en: Practically speaking, though moves to the other side.
tips.kk: Practically speaking, though — екінші жағына өту.
tips.ru: Practically speaking, though — переход к другой стороне.
tips.example: Practically speaking, though, factory-made goods are often more reliable

note.en: “Made in large numbers in a factory”.

questions.followUp: Would you pay more for them?
questions.question: Are handmade things more valuable than factory-made ones?

text: I think they do. My grandparents' generation grew up with very little, so they look after everything carefully and repair things instead of replacing them. Younger people, on the other hand, tend to value experiences more than objects — they'd rather spend money on a concert or a trip than on furniture. Interestingly, though, many young people do care deeply about their phones, which are basically their whole life.

tips.en: Grew up with very little gives the reason for the difference, not just a fact.
tips.kk: Grew up with very little — айырмашылықтың себебі, жай дерек емес.
tips.ru: Grew up with very little — причина различий, а не просто факт.

tips.en: Interestingly, though adds an exception that makes the answer lively.
tips.kk: Interestingly, though — ерекшелік жауапты жанды етеді.
tips.ru: Interestingly, though — исключение делает ответ живым.
tips.example: Interestingly, though, many young people do care deeply about their phones

note.en: “Things you do more than things you own”.
